notice: RN bank batch 138: Maternity case studies: newborn assessment, pathologic jaundice, neonatal opioid withdrawal and postpartum infection, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: A newborn in the nursery has new findings at 18 hours of age. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely condition in the middle, two actions to take now on the left and two parameters to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Notify the provider and obtain a blood culture as ordered
Start IV ampicillin and gentamicin as prescribed
Wait for the culture result before antibiotics
Give a bottle of glucose water and observe
Bathe the newborn to lower the temperature

rationale.correct: A GBS-exposed newborn with hypothermia, grunting and poor feeding needs a sepsis workup and antibiotics.

perOption.c1: GBS-positive mother without adequate prophylaxis, temperature instability and poor feeding.
perOption.c2: Does not explain temperature instability and grunting.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on neonatal sepsis.

exhibits.title: Nursery, 18 hours
exhibits.body: Mother GBS positive; antibiotic given 2 hours before birth (less than the 4 hours needed). Newborn temperature 36.1 C axillary, grunting, RR 72/min, sleepy, not latching. Glucose 42 mg/dL.

questions.stem: A client is on day 1 after a vaginal birth. For each check, choose the interpretation.

cells.text: Firm, at the umbilicus; moderate rubra
Boggy, 2 cm above and to the right; heavy rubra
1 cm below umbilicus each day; pinkish-brown serosa

options.text: Expected
Hemorrhage
Infection
Likely a full bladder; massage and help the client void
Expected
Retained placenta for certain
Expected
Subinvolution
Hemorrhage

rationale.correct: The fundus descends about 1 cm a day; a displaced boggy fundus suggests a full bladder.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.educationalObjective: Evaluate a postpartum fundus and lochia trend.

questions.stem: On a labor and delivery unit, four clients call at once. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client at 39 weeks in early labor who wants an epidural now
A client on magnesium for preeclampsia whose respiratory rate is 10/min and reflexes are absent
A client 2 hours after birth whose fundus is firm and who is asking for a meal
A client at 40 weeks whose membranes ruptured with clear fluid and a reassuring FHR

rationale.correct: Respiratory depression with absent reflexes on magnesium is the priority.

perOption.b: Magnesium toxicity with respiratory depression is life-threatening.
perOption.d: Needs assessment soon but is stable.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN has four mother-baby couplets this morning and a UAP to help. Which tasks are appropriate to hand to the UAP? Select all that apply.

options.text: Measure vital signs on a stable client on day 1
Help a client to the bathroom for the first time with the RN's guidance
Change perineal pads and report heavy bleeding
Assess the fundus and lochia of a client who just had a hemorrhage
Teach a first-time mother how to latch the baby
Give the Rho(D) immune globulin injection

rationale.correct: UAPs measure, help and report; assessment, teaching and medicines stay with the RN.

content.template: With an Apgar of 6, the nurse should {{b1}}, because cold stress can cause {{b2}}.

questions.stem: Which parts of the phototherapy plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Cover the eyes with eye shields
Leave the skin uncovered except for a small diaper
Check temperature often
Feed every 2 to 3 hours and count diapers
Apply lotion to protect the skin
Keep the baby under the lights for every feeding

questions.stem: Four hours later, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the provider at once
Prepare for IV immune globulin or exchange transfusion as ordered
Continue intensive phototherapy
Stop phototherapy because it is not working
Let the newborn sleep through the next feeding

rationale.correct: A rising level with a high-pitched cry and arching are early encephalopathy signs.

perOption.a: Rising despite phototherapy with neurologic signs.

questions.stem: For each statement, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate.

rows.text: Methadone withdrawal usually starts 24 to 72 hours or later after birth

Rooming-in with the mother reduces the need for medicine
The mother should stop methadone after birth

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
